quote: He sent me back a scan of Tversky and Kahneman
content: Replication check: the most famous demonstration in Tversky and Kahneman's 1973 availability paper has no successful replication. People judged that letters such as K and R occur more often in the first position of words than the third. Sedlmeier, Hertwig & Gigerenzer (1998) report that an earlier replication attempt failed, as did their own. With a representative sample of letters, frequency judgments closely tracked the actual frequencies. The availability heuristic as a general idea has other support, but the paper that converted the author did not survive intact.
